120|## 5. Contracts and tripwires
121|
122|A contract is one JSON file per service version. Deployments supply parameters only. Full schema: `contracts/schema.json` (D1).
123|
124|```json
125|{
126|  "service": "alert-ingestion",
127|  "version": "1.0.0",
128|  "parameters": {
129|    "expectedAlertsPerHour": { "type": "number", "required": true },
130|    "intervalSeconds": { "type": "integer", "required": true }
131|  },
132|  "components": [
133|    { "id": "connector", "kind": "connectorInstance",
134|      "logs": { "container_name": "python", "match": ["connector_name", "connector_instance"], "deploymentBy": "labels.connector_instance" } },
135|    { "id": "ingestion", "kind": "etlFlow",
136|      "logs": { "container_name": "etl", "match": ["correlation_id"], "deploymentBy": "jsonPayload.environment" } }
137|  ],
138|  "tripwires": [
139|    { "id": "dead-connector", "component": "connector", "type": "cadence",
140|      "spec": { "event": "connector.run.completed", "intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}", "maxSilentIntervals": 3 } },
141|    { "id": "canary", "component": "ingestion", "type": "synthetic",
142|      "spec": { "everyMinutes": 10, "deadlineSeconds": 180 } },
143|    { "id": "priority-shape", "component": "ingestion", "type": "schema",
144|      "spec": { "event": "alert.ingested", "field": "jsonPayload.alert.priority", "type": "integer", "enum": [-1, 40, 60, 80, 100], "required": true, "consecutive": 1, "recoverAfter": 20 } },
145|    { "id": "connector-errors", "component": "connector", "type": "errorSignature",
146|      "spec": { "minSeverity": "WARNING", "windowRuns": 10, "threshold": 8 } }
147|  ],
148|  "changePoint": { "durationSeconds": 1800, "overrides": { "dead-connector": { "maxSilentIntervals": 2 } } },
149|  "provenance": { "authoredBy": "<model id>", "scorecard": "<run id>", "approvedBy": "<human>" }
150|}
151|```
152|
153|Values were settled in D1; `contracts/*.json` is authoritative and this example matches it. The `intel-sync` contract has one `jobInstance` component and three tripwires: `dead-job` (cadence on `job.run.completed`, 3 silent intervals), `hollow-run` (schema on `job.run.completed` entries whose `status` is `SUCCESS`: `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` ≥ 1, tripping after 3 consecutive violations and recovering after 2 valid runs) and `job-errors` (errorSignature, 2 ERROR runs in the last 3).
154|
155|**Contract rules settled in D1.**
156|
157|- `logs.deploymentBy` names the entry field that identifies the deployment: `labels.connector_instance` for connectors, and the invented `jsonPayload.environment` for jobs and ETL. Google's documented job label (`job_name`) names the job definition, which is the same on every tenant, and ETL entries carry only `correlation_id`.
158|- Cadence specs name their interval explicitly (`"intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}"`).
159|- Schema tripwires take `event` (only entries with that `jsonPayload.event` are checked), `where` (equality filters on other fields), `consecutive` (violations in a row to trip; default 1) and `recoverAfter` (valid entries in a row to recover; default `consecutive`). Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset either run.
160|- For `errorSignature`, a run is one `runId`, its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when it completes (the component's cadence heartbeat). It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are at or above `minSeverity`, and recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
161|- Entering a change point re-arms cadence from that moment: a heartbeat from before the change point never counts.
162|- Cadence goes by the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, not the last entry to arrive, and trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`. It recovers on the first heartbeat that clears that condition.
163|- A canary seen exactly at its deadline is in time. A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next canary seen in time does.
164|- `load_contract` rejects a bad contract with a `ContractError` code (table in `deliverables.md` §D1).
165|
166|| Tripwire type | Checks | Trips when | Failure it catches |
167|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
168|| `cadence` | A named heartbeat event (connector run, job run) against the deployment's interval | No event for N intervals | A stopped connector or job. Runs happen on schedule regardless of alert volume, so quiet tenants do not false-alarm |
169|| `synthetic` | A planted canary alert traced end to end by `correlation_id` | The canary misses its deadline | End-to-end breakage with a healthy-looking status |
170|| `schema` | Field presence, type and allowed values on ingested events | A required field is missing, the wrong type, or out of range | Silent type breakage that volume checks miss |
171|| `errorSignature` | WARNING/ERROR rate in a component's logs over the last N runs | Count ≥ threshold | A per-tenant credential Green Liar, without planting anything in the client's SIEM |
172|
173|**Canary scope.** In the demo the canary is planted in the fake upstream per tenant. In production, planting into a client's workspace is off the table, so the canary runs on one MSSP-owned canary tenant per service version (proves the code path), and `errorSignature` covers per-tenant credential failures.

175|### 5.1 Chaos harness and scorecard
176|
177|- **Scenario library** (`fixtures/scenarios/<service>/*.yaml`, human-authored): fleet, duration, fault schedule, expected trips with a maximum detection latency, and `mustNotTrip`.
178|- **Replay**: the mock world generates each scenario's log stream on a `SimClock`; the stream runs through the evaluator. No GCP, seconds per run.
179|- **Scorecard**: per scenario, expected versus actual trips, detection latency, false positives. A contract passes only at 100% expected trips and zero false positives.
180|- **The SRE never writes scenarios or expected outcomes.** It sees scorecard results only.
181|- **Held-out scenarios.** Some scenarios are marked `holdout: true`. They never appear in revision feedback, not even by ID. A contract passes only if the holdouts pass too; when only a holdout fails, the feedback says "a held-out scenario failed" and nothing more. This stops the authoring loop from fitting the visible scenarios.

183|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
184|
185|### 6.1 The loop
186|
187|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
188|
189|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
190|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
191|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
192|- **Ending.**
193|
194|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
195|| --- | --- | --- |
196|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
197|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
198|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
199|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
200|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
201|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
202|| The same read call a third time in a segment | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
203|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
204|
205|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
206|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
207|
208|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
209|
210|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped per segment: 12 in the first, 4 more after each resume. A read over the cap is refused with an error, and the loop continues. A component that is not one of the service's component IDs is refused rather than answered with empty data.
211|
212|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
213|| --- | --- | --- |
214|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
215|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
216|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
217|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
218|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
219|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
220|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
221|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |
222|
223|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
224|
225|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Each problem starts with the rule it broke (`evidence.value: …`); the rule codes are listed in `docs/d5-pins.md`. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
226|
227|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
228|| --- | --- | --- |
229|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
230|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
231|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
232|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |

249|### 6.5 Diagnosis schema and submission rules
250|
251|```json
252|{
253|  "incidentId": "string",
254|  "deployment": "string",
255|  "component": "string",
256|  "category": "connector_stalled | job_stalled | credential_failure | schema_drift | job_hollow_success | job_failing | unknown",
257|  "hypothesis": "ID of the hypothesis the SRE concludes (from set_hypotheses)",
258|  "summary": "the conclusion in one or two sentences",
259|  "evidence": ["E1", "E3"],
260|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
261|  "action": {
262|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
263|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
264|    "resource": "full resource name",
265|    "updateMask": ["field"],
266|    "patch": {},
267|    "escalationSummary": "string, when type is escalate"
268|  },
269|  "expectedVerification": { "tripwire": "string", "condition": "recovers_within", "seconds": 0 },
270|  "rollback": "string",
271|  "confidence": "low | medium | high"
272|}
273|```
274|
275|`category` is an enum so evaluations grade deterministically. The tool schema sets `additionalProperties: false` throughout.
276|
277|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
278|
279|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
280|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
281|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.
282|4. **Category evidence rule.** The cited evidence includes what the category requires (table below).
283|5. **Action.** `propose`: the method is in §6.4, `updateMask` is within its allowed fields, the patch keys are within `updateMask`, and `resource` is the deployment's own connector instance (`connectorInstances.*`) or job instance (`jobInstances.*`). `propose` and `none`: `expectedVerification.tripwire` is a tripwire of the incident's deployment. `none`: at least one cited item was recorded after the session's most recent resume. `escalate`: `escalationSummary` is not empty.
284|
285|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.
286|
287|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.
288|
289|| Category | Cited evidence must include |
290|| --- | --- |
291|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's latest `connector.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
292|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's latest `job.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
293|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result for the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false` |
294|| `schema_drift` | An entry of the deployment that violates one of its schema tripwires |
295|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0` |
296|| `job_failing` | A `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` entry with `status: ERROR` |
297|| `unknown` | Nothing, but the action must be `escalate` |

299|### 6.6 Guardrails
300|
301|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
302|- **Budgets.** Per segment of an investigation (the first run, then each resume): 24 turns, 12 read calls and 400,000 tokens (input plus output) at first, then `extra_turns` and 4 read calls per resume; all configurable. Two remediation attempts per incident.
303|- **Stuck detection.** The same read tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time in a segment pauses the session with reason `stuck` before the call runs. Working tools are exempt: repeating one changes state, and repeated refused submissions reach the refusal cap.
304|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
305|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.
306|- **Recorded replay.** Live investigations chosen as fixtures (`fixtures/recorded/`) replay offline in CI through the scripted transport. Any difference in tool calls, gate verdicts or the final diagnosis blocks the merge.
307|- **Model calls.** Exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s) on 429 and 5xx; a 120 s request timeout counts as a 5xx; diagnoses cached on the public instance; spend caps.
308|- **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may not import GCP clients or the Chronicle client directly; it reaches the world only through the tool set.

442|1. **Replay loop.** One `SimClock` is shared by World and Evaluator; faults go through `world.schedule` with `at`/`clearAt` offsets from t0. 443|2. **Deployments.** Scenario `deployments` are environment names; deployment IDs are `<service>/<environment>`. A scorecard runs a contract against its own service's scenarios only, held-out ones included.

Trip latency counts from the latest fault `at` on that environment at or before the event; recovery latency from the latest `clearAt` (the fault `at` when there is none). An event after `withinSeconds`, or before the fault, is missing and also unexpected.
445|4. **False positives** are strict: every unmatched actual trip or recovery is `unexpected`. `expected_hit_rate` = matched expected trips and recoveries / all of them (1.0 when there are none). `mustNotTrip` entries are asserted but are not expected items.

448|7. **Cadence** uses the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, never the last entry to arrive.
449|8. **Isolation** (T8) compares (kind, deployment, tripwire) only, never `runId` or `insertId`, which are global counters.

451|10. **Change point.** Overrides take the contract's `changePoint.overrides` shape; cadence re-arms at entry; overrides revert after `duration_s`. The executor calls `enter_change_point(deployment, component, duration_s=..., overrides=contract.changePoint.overrides)` after an approved change (D6).

34|- one `ScriptedTransport` list cannot route responses to incidents;

442|1. **Replay loop.** One `SimClock` is shared by World and Evaluator; faults go through `world.schedule` with `at`/`clearAt` offsets from t0. At each tick instant, as built: `scheduler.tick()`, `world.step_until(t)`, ingest every new sink entry in write order, `evaluator.tick()`. A canary planted at a tick can be fetched by a run at the same instant.
443|2. **Deployments.** Scenario `deployments` are environment names; deployment IDs are `<service>/<environment>`. A scorecard runs a contract against its own service's scenarios only, held-out ones included.
444|3. **Matching and latency.** Actual events match expected ones on (deployment, tripwire). Trip latency counts from the latest fault `at` on that environment at or before the event; recovery latency from the latest `clearAt` (the fault `at` when there is none). An event after `withinSeconds`, or before the fault, is missing and also unexpected.
445|4. **False positives** are strict: every unmatched actual trip or recovery is `unexpected`. `expected_hit_rate` = matched expected trips and recoveries / all of them (1.0 when there are none). `mustNotTrip` entries are asserted but are not expected items.
446|5. **Routing.** Entries route to a deployment by the component's `container_name` and `match` labels, then `deploymentBy`; a connector label maps through `Deployment.resources`, with `jsonPayload.environment` as the fallback.
447|6. **Arming.** `${param}` is resolved when a deployment is armed. Cadence and canary are evaluated in `tick()`, schema and errorSignature in `ingest()`. Every `TripEvent.at` is `clock.now()`. The evaluator keeps only the runs a window needs.
448|7. **Cadence** uses the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, never the last entry to arrive.
449|8. **Isolation** (T8) compares (kind, deployment, tripwire) only, never `runId` or `insertId`, which are global counters.
450|9. **Canary scheduler** plants through `World.plant_canary`, first at arm + `everyMinutes`, then every `everyMinutes`, only for deployments whose contract has a synthetic tripwire.
451|10. **Change point.** Overrides take the contract's `changePoint.overrides` shape; cadence re-arms at entry; overrides revert after `duration_s`. The executor calls `enter_change_point(deployment, component, duration_s=..., overrides=contract.changePoint.overrides)` after an approved change (D6).
452|11. **Cost.** The scenario-library tests share module-scoped scorecards.
453|12. **Known weakness.** With errorSignature recovery after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs, `flap-severe` (rate 0.7) passes on its seed partly by luck: about 2 seeds in 3 would see a 3-clean streak and a recovery. A symmetric rule (recover when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are clean) is more robust; deferred until after the hackathon.

27|## 1. Summary
28|
29|Fleet SRE is an agentic site reliability engineer for MSSPs running multi-tenant Google SecOps SOAR. It writes each service's monitoring contract, investigates when a tripwire fires and proposes a fix for a human to approve. The platform underneath exists only to give it safe tools and deterministic checks.
30|
31|- **Problem.** An MSSP runs many tenants (SOAR environments) across many services in one instance. Connectors fail silently, a `LIVE` status can sit on a connector that ingests nothing, and each tenant's monitoring depends on who onboarded it.
32|- **What the SRE does.** Authors one contract per service version, investigates incidents with read-only tools and proposes allowlisted actions. The platform writes the postmortem from the incident record. Drafting contract amendments is designed but cut (§9).
33|- **Why it can be trusted.** It isn't. Deterministic code grades every output: contracts by a chaos scorecard, evidence when it is recorded, diagnoses when they are submitted, fixes by tripwires.
34|- **Fleet leverage.** Amendments land on the service contract, so one tenant's incident hardens every tenant on that service. (Designed; the amendment step is cut, §9.)
35|- **Built on.** A local-first Python system with a mock SecOps built against Google's published Chronicle API and SOAR log format, with Cloud Logging and IAM on a personal GCP project (Pub/Sub, Cloud Run and Firestore are cut, §9).
36|- **Entry.** Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Indie track, "Build for Your World" theme. Submission due 2026-11-04 at 9:00 PM ET.
37|
38|## 2. Design principles
39|
40|1. **Verified, not trusted.** Every SRE output has a deterministic check: a contract must pass the chaos scorecard, evidence must exist when it is recorded, a diagnosis must rest on recorded evidence of the right kind, a fix must pass change-point tripwires.
41|2. **Reason once, run cheap.** The model works when a contract is written or amended and when an incident opens. No model sits in the watch loop.
42|3. **One contract per service.** The contract versions with the service definition. Per-tenant differences are parameters. The platform uses whatever integration version is installed; upgrades are a separate process.
43|4. **Every incident hardens every tenant.** Amendments land on the service contract, so a gap found on one tenant closes for all of them.
44|5. **The agent holds no credentials.** Read tools are proxied by the platform under a read-only identity; writes need human approval and run under a separate identity. IAM enforces this and tests prove it.
45|6. **Built against Google's spec.** Mock resources and log labels copy the published Chronicle API and SOAR logging docs, so the mock can be swapped for a real instance. What is invented is labelled as invented (see `mocks.md` §9).
46|7. **Local first.** Everything runs on a laptop with `make demo`. GCP services are adapters behind ports, swapped in late.
47|8. **The same rule applies to the build.** Humans write what defines correctness (contracts, scenarios, expected outcomes, acceptance test specs, SRE prompts in `prompts/`). The coding agent writes what is graded against them.
48|9. **Checks live inside the tools.** A gate runs inside the tool that moves work forward (recording evidence, submitting a diagnosis), never as a separate tool the model may choose to call, because a confident model skips optional checks. A refused call comes back as an error the model reads and fixes. The model chooses every call; code never hard-codes the order.
49|
50|Field lessons that shape the tripwires: absence-only detection cannot tell quiet from broken, and a field changing type (severity arriving as a string) passes every volume check.
51|
52|## 3. The SRE loop
53|
54|The model acts at two points (author, investigate); closing is deterministic (step 7). Deterministic code grades each output before anything changes; inside an investigation, the gates sit in the tools (§6.1).
55|
56|```mermaid
57|flowchart LR
58|  A["Write contract (SRE)"] --> B["Chaos scorecard"] --> C{"Passes?"}
59|  C -- "no: revise" --> A
60|  C -- "yes" --> D["Approve contract (human)"] --> E["Tripwires watch"]
61|  E -- "tripwire fires" --> F["Investigate (SRE)"]
62|  F -- "escalates or hits a limit" --> N["Needs input (human)"]
63|  N -- "reply, more turns, or fault state changed" --> F
64|  F -- "proposes action" --> G["Approve fix (human)"]
65|  G -- "rejected with notes" --> F
66|  G -- "approved" --> H["Apply fix (deployer identity)"] --> I{"Verified?"}
67|  F -- "no action: verify recovery" --> I
68|  I -- "no: retry, max 2, then escalate" --> F
69|  I -- "yes" --> J["Close incident (postmortem)"]
70|  J -. "gap found: amend (cut)" .-> A
71|```
72|
73|1. **Author.** Given a service brief, sample logs and parameters, the SRE drafts a contract. The harness scores it; the SRE revises against the scorecard (max 3 revisions); a human approves.
74|2. **Watch.** The evaluator runs every deployment's tripwires. No model call.
75|3. **Investigate.** A trip opens an incident. The SRE states hypotheses, investigates with read tools, records evidence that is checked as it is recorded, and submits a diagnosis through a gated tool (§6.1). The diagnosis proposes one action, proposes no action and asks for verification, or escalates.
76|4. **Hand off.** An escalation, or an investigation that hits a limit, pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT. No model calls are made while it waits. It resumes the same session only when something changed: a human replied, more turns were granted, or the incident's tripwire state changed (for example, a credential was rotated outside the platform).
77|5. **Approve and apply.** A human sees hypotheses, evidence and the patch diff, and approves or rejects with notes; notes go back to the SRE as its next message. On approval the executor journals its intent, then applies the change under the deployer identity.
78|6. **Verify.** A change-point window tightens checks on that component. The diagnosis states the expected outcome; the tripwires decide. Failure returns to investigation at most twice, then escalates.
79|7. **Close and learn.** The platform writes the postmortem from the incident record: timeline, pauses and what resumed them, category, action and transcripts. Amendment (the SRE drafts a contract change after a late or missing trip; it is rescored, approved and applied to every deployment of the service) is designed but cut (§9).

120|## 5. Contracts and tripwires
121|
122|A contract is one JSON file per service version. Deployments supply parameters only. Full schema: `contracts/schema.json` (D1).
123|
124|```json
125|{
126|  "service": "alert-ingestion",
127|  "version": "1.0.0",
128|  "parameters": {
129|    "expectedAlertsPerHour": { "type": "number", "required": true },
130|    "intervalSeconds": { "type": "integer", "required": true }
131|  },
132|  "components": [
133|    { "id": "connector", "kind": "connectorInstance",
134|      "logs": { "container_name": "python", "match": ["connector_name", "connector_instance"], "deploymentBy": "labels.connector_instance" } },
135|    { "id": "ingestion", "kind": "etlFlow",
136|      "logs": { "container_name": "etl", "match": ["correlation_id"], "deploymentBy": "jsonPayload.environment" } }
137|  ],
138|  "tripwires": [
139|    { "id": "dead-connector", "component": "connector", "type": "cadence",
140|      "spec": { "event": "connector.run.completed", "intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}", "maxSilentIntervals": 3 } },
141|    { "id": "canary", "component": "ingestion", "type": "synthetic",
142|      "spec": { "everyMinutes": 10, "deadlineSeconds": 180 } },
143|    { "id": "priority-shape", "component": "ingestion", "type": "schema",
144|      "spec": { "event": "alert.ingested", "field": "jsonPayload.alert.priority", "type": "integer", "enum": [-1, 40, 60, 80, 100], "required": true, "consecutive": 1, "recoverAfter": 20 } },
145|    { "id": "connector-errors", "component": "connector", "type": "errorSignature",
146|      "spec": { "minSeverity": "WARNING", "windowRuns": 10, "threshold": 8 } }
147|  ],
148|  "changePoint": { "durationSeconds": 1800, "overrides": { "dead-connector": { "maxSilentIntervals": 2 } } },
149|  "provenance": { "authoredBy": "<model id>", "scorecard": "<run id>", "approvedBy": "<human>" }
150|}
151|```
152|
153|Values were settled in D1; `contracts/*.json` is authoritative and this example matches it. The `intel-sync` contract has one `jobInstance` component and three tripwires: `dead-job` (cadence on `job.run.completed`, 3 silent intervals), `hollow-run` (schema on `job.run.completed` entries whose `status` is `SUCCESS`: `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` ≥ 1, tripping after 3 consecutive violations and recovering after 2 valid runs) and `job-errors` (errorSignature, 2 ERROR runs in the last 3).
154|
155|**Contract rules settled in D1.**
156|
157|- `logs.deploymentBy` names the entry field that identifies the deployment: `labels.connector_instance` for connectors, and the invented `jsonPayload.environment` for jobs and ETL. Google's documented job label (`job_name`) names the job definition, which is the same on every tenant, and ETL entries carry only `correlation_id`.
158|- Cadence specs name their interval explicitly (`"intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}"`).
159|- Schema tripwires take `event` (only entries with that `jsonPayload.event` are checked), `where` (equality filters on other fields), `consecutive` (violations in a row to trip; default 1) and `recoverAfter` (valid entries in a row to recover; default `consecutive`). Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset either run.
160|- For `errorSignature`, a run is one `runId`, its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when it completes (the component's cadence heartbeat). It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are at or above `minSeverity`, and recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
161|- Entering a change point re-arms cadence from that moment: a heartbeat from before the change point never counts.
162|- Cadence goes by the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, not the last entry to arrive, and trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`. It recovers on the first heartbeat that clears that condition.
163|- A canary seen exactly at its deadline is in time. A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next canary seen in time does.
164|- `load_contract` rejects a bad contract with a `ContractError` code (table in `deliverables.md` §D1).
165|
166|| Tripwire type | Checks | Trips when | Failure it catches |
167|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
168|| `cadence` | A named heartbeat event (connector run, job run) against the deployment's interval | No event for N intervals | A stopped connector or job. Runs happen on schedule regardless of alert volume, so quiet tenants do not false-alarm |
169|| `synthetic` | A planted canary alert traced end to end by `correlation_id` | The canary misses its deadline | End-to-end breakage with a healthy-looking status |
170|| `schema` | Field presence, type and allowed values on ingested events | A required field is missing, the wrong type, or out of range | Silent type breakage that volume checks miss |
171|| `errorSignature` | WARNING/ERROR rate in a component's logs over the last N runs | Count ≥ threshold | A per-tenant credential Green Liar, without planting anything in the client's SIEM |
172|
173|**Canary scope.** In the demo the canary is planted in the fake upstream per tenant. In production, planting into a client's workspace is off the table, so the canary runs on one MSSP-owned canary tenant per service version (proves the code path), and `errorSignature` covers per-tenant credential failures.
174|
175|### 5.1 Chaos harness and scorecard
176|
177|- **Scenario library** (`fixtures/scenarios/<service>/*.yaml`, human-authored): fleet, duration, fault schedule, expected trips with a maximum detection latency, and `mustNotTrip`.
178|- **Replay**: the mock world generates each scenario's log stream on a `SimClock`; the stream runs through the evaluator. No GCP, seconds per run.
179|- **Scorecard**: per scenario, expected versus actual trips, detection latency, false positives. A contract passes only at 100% expected trips and zero false positives.
180|- **The SRE never writes scenarios or expected outcomes.** It sees scorecard results only.
181|- **Held-out scenarios.** Some scenarios are marked `holdout: true`. They never appear in revision feedback, not even by ID. A contract passes only if the holdouts pass too; when only a holdout fails, the feedback says "a held-out scenario failed" and nothing more. This stops the authoring loop from fitting the visible scenarios.
182|
183|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
184|
185|### 6.1 The loop
186|
187|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
188|
189|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
190|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
191|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
192|- **Ending.**
193|
194|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
195|| --- | --- | --- |
196|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
197|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
198|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
199|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
200|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
201|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
202|| The same read call a third time in a segment | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
203|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
204|
205|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
206|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
207|
208|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
209|
210|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped per segment: 12 in the first, 4 more after each resume. A read over the cap is refused with an error, and the loop continues. A component that is not one of the service's component IDs is refused rather than answered with empty data.
211|
212|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
213|| --- | --- | --- |
214|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
215|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
216|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
217|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
218|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
219|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
220|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
221|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |
222|
223|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
224|
225|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Each problem starts with the rule it broke (`evidence.value: …`); the rule codes are listed in `docs/d5-pins.md`. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
226|
227|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
228|| --- | --- | --- |
229|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
230|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
231|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
232|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |
233|
234|### 6.4 Action allowlist
235|
236|| Action | Notes |
237|| --- | --- |
238|| `connectorInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `intervalSeconds`, `parameters` |
239|| `connectorInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
240|| `connectorInstances.runOnDemand` | |
241|| `jobInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `parameters` |
242|| `jobInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
243|| `jobInstances.runOnDemand` | |
244|| `none` | No write: the fault has cleared (for example, after a human acted on an escalation). Goes straight to verification |
245|| `escalate` | Required when the fix is outside the allowlist (e.g. a credential rotation). Pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT |
246|
247|`connectorInstances.setLogsCollection` is not an action: turning on logging fixes nothing, so verification would fail it. The SRE can ask for it in an `escalationSummary`.

249|### 6.5 Diagnosis schema and submission rules
250|
251|```json
252|{
253|  "incidentId": "string",
254|  "deployment": "string",
255|  "component": "string",
256|  "category": "connector_stalled | job_stalled | credential_failure | schema_drift | job_hollow_success | job_failing | unknown",
257|  "hypothesis": "ID of the hypothesis the SRE concludes (from set_hypotheses)",
258|  "summary": "the conclusion in one or two sentences",
259|  "evidence": ["E1", "E3"],
260|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
261|  "action": {
262|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
263|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
264|    "resource": "full resource name",
265|    "updateMask": ["field"],
266|    "patch": {},
267|    "escalationSummary": "string, when type is escalate"
268|  },
269|  "expectedVerification": { "tripwire": "string", "condition": "recovers_within", "seconds": 0 },
270|  "rollback": "string",
271|  "confidence": "low | medium | high"
272|}
273|```
274|
275|`category` is an enum so evaluations grade deterministically. The tool schema sets `additionalProperties: false` throughout.
276|
277|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
278|
279|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
280|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
281|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.
282|4. **Category evidence rule.** The cited evidence includes what the category requires (table below).
283|5. **Action.** `propose`: the method is in §6.4, `updateMask` is within its allowed fields, the patch keys are within `updateMask`, and `resource` is the deployment's own connector instance (`connectorInstances.*`) or job instance (`jobInstances.*`). `propose` and `none`: `expectedVerification.tripwire` is a tripwire of the incident's deployment. `none`: at least one cited item was recorded after the session's most recent resume. `escalate`: `escalationSummary` is not empty.
284|
285|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.
286|
287|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.
288|
289|| Category | Cited evidence must include |
290|| --- | --- |
291|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's latest `connector.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
292|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's latest `job.run.completed` entry at or before the trip (that exact entry) |
293|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result for the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false` |
294|| `schema_drift` | An entry of the deployment that violates one of its schema tripwires |
295|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0` |
296|| `job_failing` | A `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` entry with `status: ERROR` |
297|| `unknown` | Nothing, but the action must be `escalate` |
298|
299|### 6.6 Guardrails
300|
301|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
302|- **Budgets.** Per segment of an investigation (the first run, then each resume): 24 turns, 12 read calls and 400,000 tokens (input plus output) at first, then `extra_turns` and 4 read calls per resume; all configurable. Two remediation attempts per incident.
303|- **Stuck detection.** The same read tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time in a segment pauses the session with reason `stuck` before the call runs. Working tools are exempt: repeating one changes state, and repeated refused submissions reach the refusal cap.
304|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
305|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.
306|- **Recorded replay.** Live investigations chosen as fixtures (`fixtures/recorded/`) replay offline in CI through the scripted transport. Any difference in tool calls, gate verdicts or the final diagnosis blocks the merge.
307|- **Model calls.** Exponential backoff (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s) on 429 and 5xx; a 120 s request timeout counts as a 5xx; diagnoses cached on the public instance; spend caps.
308|- **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may not import GCP clients or the Chronicle client directly; it reaches the world only through the tool set.
309|
310|## 7. Identity and IAM
311|
312|| Identity | Grants | Must not be able to |
313|| --- | --- | --- |
314|| `obs-reader` (evaluator, SRE read tools) | `roles/logging.viewer`; `roles/pubsub.subscriber` on the one subscription; read permissions on the mock API | Write logs; call mock write methods |
315|| `deployer` (executor) | Write permissions on the mock API | Read the subscription; act without an approval record |
316|| `mock-soar` (mock SecOps runtime) | `roles/logging.logWriter` | Anything else |
317|| SRE (model) | None | Call GCP or the mock API directly |
318|
319|No service-account keys. Locally: impersonation. Cloud Run: attached service accounts. The mock verifies the caller's Google ID token and maps the service-account email to Chronicle-style permissions (`chronicle.connectorInstances.get`, `chronicle.connectorInstanceLogs.get`, ...). Tests: positive paths, negative 403s, exact permission sets via `testIamPermissions`, and no user-managed keys (`deliverables.md` D7).
320|
321|## 8. Model usage
322|
323|One gateway, per-role config. Assignments are provisional until the D2 spike and the D5 live eval.
324|
325|| Role | Frequency | Starting model | Reasoning effort |
326|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
327|| Author / amend contracts | Rare | `muse-wonder-1.0` via Meta Model API | `high` |
328|| Investigate / propose | Per incident | `muse-spark-1.3` via Meta Model API | `medium` |
329|| Postmortem | — | None: built from the incident record (D6a) | — |
330|| Fallback | On rate limits | Muse Spark Open from a partner, if credits arrive: Baseten `meta-models/muse-spark-open` (base URL `https://inference.baseten.co/v1`) or Fireworks `accounts/fireworks/models/muse-spark-open` | `medium` |
331|| Building the project | Throughout | Muse Code | — |
332|
333|**API details** (from Meta's cookbooks):
334|
335|- **Endpoint and key.** Base URL `https://api.meta.ai/v1`. The key lives in `MODEL_API_KEY` and is passed explicitly; the OpenAI SDK does not read that variable on its own.
336|- **Investigation loop.** Responses API with `store=False` and the full history sent every turn, `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` so reasoning is replayed between turns, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, and `reasoning={"effort": ...}` per role. Effort levels: `none` < `minimal` < `low` < `medium` < `high` (`xhigh` is the same as `high`).
337|- **JSON outside tools** (authoring). On the Responses API use `text.format` with a JSON schema; `response_format` returns HTTP 400 there. A recursive `$ref` also returns 400, so the schema given to the authoring model must be flattened. `strict: true` returns 400 on keywords the contract schema uses (`minProperties`), so `strict` is omitted and the contract loader is the real check (D6b P1).
338|- **Prompt caching.** Keep the stable prefix first (system prompt, tool specs, contract) and record `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` in the transcript (field names confirmed in D2).
339|- **Cost.** Muse Spark is billed against the $150 credit on this account (D2: about $0.08 per investigation at ~120k input tokens, ~70% cached; D5: at most about $0.10 per investigation at ~130k input tokens, ~74% cached). Muse Wonder (authoring, effort `high`): about $0.13 and 48 s for a first version at ~7k input and ~5k output tokens (D6b P1). Baseten, Modal and Fireworks each offer $100 to select participants for open-weights models.
340|
341|Muse Code bills the same $150 credit (verified by usage delta).

Read text file `docs/d5-pins.md`.
1|# D5 pins
2|
3|Interfaces and semantics of the D5 investigator as built (PRs #22–#27). `deliverables.md` §D5 and `spec.md` §6 summarise them; this file has the detail and wins where they differ. `tests/acceptance/d5/` encodes the testable rules; `tests/unit/` covers the rest.
4|
5|## Interfaces
6|
7|1. **`fleetsre/ports.py`.**
8|   - `LogQuery` protocol: `entries(start, end) -> list[LogEntry]`, `get(insert_id) -> LogEntry | None`; `MemoryLogQuery(sink)`.
9|   - `ChronicleClient` protocol: `get(name)`, `list_connector_logs(name, page_size)`, `list_job_logs(name, page_size)`, `execute_test(name)`, `patch(name, body, update_mask)`, `run_on_demand(name, body)`, `set_logs_collection(name, enabled)`, and an `identity` attribute. Returns parsed JSON or raises `ChronicleError(status, body)` carrying the Google error body.
10|   - `StateStore` protocol: `record_trip(event)`, `record_change(deployment, record)`, `trip_history(deployment) -> list[dict]`; `MemoryStateStore`.
11|2. **`fleetsre/adapters/chronicle_http.py`.** `ChronicleHttpClient(http: httpx.Client, identity: str)` sends `X-Fleetsre-Identity` (dev auth; ID tokens come in D7).
12|3. **`fleetsre/registry.py`.**
13|   - `Registry(contracts, deployments, scorecards=None)` with `contract(service)`, `deployments(service)`, `deployment(id)`, `scorecard(service)` and `route(entry) -> list[(deployment ID, component ID)]`, using the evaluator's routing (D4 semantics item 5). D6 adds `apply_contract`.
14|   - `Deployment.resource_names` maps component ID → full Chronicle resource name, plus `"integrationInstance"`. `deployments_from_fleet` computes it from the fleet; `Deployment.resources` keeps its D4 meaning (routing).
15|4. **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may import `fleetsre.registry`, `contracts`, `logmodel`, `ports`, `clock` and `evaluator.tripwires`. It must not reach `google`, `fleetsre.adapters` or `fleetsre.mock`, transitively included. `.importlinter` sets `exclude_type_checking_imports = True`.
16|5. **`ToolSet(log_query, chronicle, state, registry, *, clock, verification=True)`.**
17|   - `call(name, args, session, *, call_id=None)` always returns `{"callId": <id>, "result": <dict>}`: exactly what reaches the model.
18|   - A refusal's result is `{"error": str, "problems": [str]}`. `call` never raises; an internal error is a refusal with rule `tool.error`.
19|   - With `call_id=None` the ToolSet assigns `local-<n>`.
20|   - Every call is stored in `session.calls[call_id]` as a `CallRecord(tool, args, result, verdict, problems, turn)`.
21|   - The gates get the incident through `Incident.reconstruct(session.incident_id, registry, now)`, which parses the ID against the registry's services, environments and tripwire IDs (never by splitting on `-`).
22|   - Read-tool output schemas live in `fleetsre/sre/schemas.py` as `READ_TOOL_OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`.
23|6. **`Incident`** has `id`, `deployment`, `tripwire`, `opened_at`, `trip_event`, `service`, `component`, `resources` and `siblings`.
24|   - `resources` comes from `Deployment.resource_names`; `siblings` holds deployment IDs.
25|   - `Incident.from_trip(event, registry, now)` sets `id = f"inc-{service}-{environment}-{tripwire}-{at:%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ}"`.
26|   - `render_incident(incident, registry) -> str` builds the first user message: incident ID, deployment, `Component: <ID> (the tripped tripwire's component)`, every component of the service with its kind and full resource name, every tripwire with its component, the tripped tripwire's type and spec with `${param}` resolved (never the description text), trip reason, trip evidence insertIds, trippedAt, now, sibling IDs and budgets.
27|7. **`Evidence`** gains `deployment: str | None`. For a log source, `value` is `entry.model_dump(mode="json")`.
28|8. **`Session`** is JSON round-trippable.
29|   - Typed fields: `hypotheses: dict[str, Hypothesis]`, `evidence: dict[str, Evidence]`, `calls: dict[str, CallRecord]`.
30|   - Also: `turn`, `history` (input items), `segment_start_turn`, `turn_limit`, `read_limit`, `token_limit`, `segment_reads`, `segment_tokens`, `refused_submissions`, `resumed_at_turns`, `transcript_id` and `plan`.
31|   - `status` is `running | submitted | needs_input`.
32|   - `SessionStore`: `save`, `load`, `append_transcript(transcript_id, record)`, `transcript(transcript_id)`. Implementations: `MemorySessionStore()` (`fleetsre/sre/session.py`) and `SqliteSessionStore(path)` (`fleetsre/adapters/sqlite_state.py`).
33|9. **`investigate(incident, tools, gateway, store, *, max_turns=24, max_read_calls=12, max_tokens=400_000)`.**
34|   - With no saved session it starts one. With a saved `running` session it continues it with the budgets passed. With a saved `submitted` or `needs_input` session it raises `ValueError`.
35|   - `resume(incident, tools, gateway, store, *, message, extra_turns=8, extra_reads=4)` raises `ValueError` unless the saved session is `needs_input`.
36|   - Both return `InvestigationResult(diagnosis, status, reason, transcript_id, turns, read_calls, tokens, refusals)`. `status` is `submitted`, with `reason` the submitted action type (`propose` or `none`), or `needs_input` with a reason from pin 15. For `escalated`, `diagnosis` is set.
37|10. **`ModelGateway(config, transport, *, sleep=time.sleep)`.**
38|    - `ModelGateway.respond(role, input_items, tools)` returns `ModelResponse(output, usage)`; `tools` may be `None`.
39|    - `Transport.create(request: dict) -> dict` raises `TransportError(status)`.
40|    - `ScriptedTransport(responses)` records `.requests`; an item `{"_error": <status>}` raises `TransportError`.
41|    - `GatewayConfig.prices`: per model, USD per 1M tokens (`input`, `cached_input`, `output`).
42|    - `OpenAITransport(*, api_key, base_url)` calls the OpenAI SDK's `responses.create` with SDK `max_retries=0` and `timeout=120`. A timeout surfaces as `TransportError(504)`. The key is passed explicitly from `MODEL_API_KEY`.
43|    - The live role comes from `FLEETSRE_INVESTIGATE_MODEL` (default `muse-spark-1.3`), effort `medium`, prices from `FLEETSRE_PRICES_JSON`.
44|11. **Gate signatures.** `check_hypotheses(items)`; `check_evidence(args, session, log_query, incident, registry)`; `check_diagnosis(d, session, incident, contract, log_query, registry)`.
45|
46|## Loop
47|
48|12. **Input.** `[developer message: prompts/investigate.md verbatim, user message: render_incident] + history`.
49|    - Request flags: `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, `reasoning={"effort": role effort}`, `tools=specs()`, `model` = role model.
50|    - Output items are replayed as returned (`exclude_none`).
51|13. **Tool outputs.** Every `function_call` gets a `function_call_output` whose `output` is the string `json.dumps({"callId", "result"})`. Only the first call in a response runs. The others get the error `not run: only the first tool call in a response runs`, and don't count as calls or toward stuck. A reply with no tool call gets the user message `Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool.` and counts as a turn.
52|14. **Last turn.** When `turn == turn_limit`, the user message `This is your last turn. Call submit_diagnosis now with what you have.` is appended before the request, after any plain-text message.
53|15. **Budgets are per segment.** The first investigation is segment 1, and each resume starts a new one.
54|    - Turns: `max_turns`, then `extra_turns`.
55|    - Reads: `max_read_calls`, then `extra_reads`. Only accepted calls to the eight read tools count. A read over the cap is refused (`reads.cap`) and still counts as a turn.
56|    - Tokens: `max_tokens`, counted from the segment start as usage input + output. The check runs after each turn; an accepted submission on that turn wins.
57|    - Three refused submissions in a segment end with `needs_input`/`refused`.
58|    - After a turn, the order is: accepted submission, then the refusal cap, then the token budget.
59|    - The refused-submission count and the stuck counts reset at each resume.
60|    - `needs_input` reasons: `escalated`, `refused`, `budget`, `token_budget`, `stuck`, `model_unavailable`.
61|16. **Stuck.** A read tool called with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time within a segment ends with `needs_input`/`stuck`, before the call runs. Only executed calls count (verdict `accepted` or `wouldRefuse`). Working tools never trip it: repeating one changes session state, and three identical refused submissions reach the refusal cap instead.
62|17. **Backoff.** 429 and 5xx retry with delays of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 s (no jitter), up to `max_retries`, then `needs_input`/`model_unavailable`. Any other `TransportError` → `model_unavailable` at once. Other exceptions propagate.
63|18. **Transcript.** One record per turn, saved with the session after every turn. Each record holds the output items, the tool, args, verdict (`accepted | refused | wouldRefuse | no_tool_call | stuck`), problems, the output, usage (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) and `cost_usd`.
64|
65|## Tools
66|
67|19. **`query_logs(deployment, window, filter, rationale)`.**
68|    - `window` is `{"lastMinutes": 1..360}`, relative to `clock.now()`.
69|    - `filter` is `{component?, event?, minSeverity?, runId?}`, `additionalProperties: false`. A `component` that is not a component ID of the deployment's contract is refused (`tool.name`), listing the valid IDs.
70|    - Returns `{"entries", "total", "truncated"}`: newest first by timestamp, at most 50. Each entry is compact: `insertId`, `timestamp`, `severity`, `labels`, `jsonPayload`, `container`.
71|    - Querying a sibling deployment marks it queried.
72|20. **`get_resource(name)`** is GET only. `name` must match an `environments`, `integrationInstances`, `connectorInstances` or `jobInstances` pattern under the fixed prefix (mocks §4.1). Anything else, including `:` custom methods and `/logs/` paths, is refused (`tool.name`) with no HTTP call. Mock errors pass through as an accepted `{"error": <Google error body>}`.
73|21. **Log and test tools.** `list_connector_logs(name)` and `list_job_logs(name)` take full resource names and return one page of 50, newest first: `{"logs", "truncated"}`. `test_integration_instance(name)` takes integration instance names only and returns the `executeTest` body.
74|22. **`compare_siblings(service, component, window)`**, where `window` is `{"lastMinutes": 1..360}` as in pin 19. For each deployment of the service it returns: runs, runs at or above WARNING, ERROR runs, the last heartbeat's timestamp and insertId, alerts ingested, and the insertId of the worst recent entry. It marks every sibling queried. An unknown component is refused (`tool.name`), listing the valid IDs.
75|23. **`tripwire_history(deployment)`** reads the `StateStore`. **`get_contract(service)`** returns the contract JSON with every tripwire `description` removed, plus a scorecard summary only (`passed`, `expected_hit_rate`, `false_positives`, `scenarios: <count>`), with no scenario IDs.
76|24. **Specs.** `submit_diagnosis` carries the full §6.5 schema with its `required` lists (diagnosis, action, `expectedVerification`, `openQuestions` items) and `condition` enum `["recovers_within"]`. `record_evidence`'s `source` is `{insertId}` or `{callId, field, value}`. Every schema has `additionalProperties: false` and a required `rationale` (`maxLength` 200). `update_plan(plan, rationale)` records the plan and has no gate.
77|
78|## Gates
79|
80|25. **Problem strings** take the form `<rule>: <text>`. Rules:
81|    - Order and hypotheses: `order`, `hypotheses.count`, `hypotheses.alternative`, `hypotheses.id`.
82|    - Evidence: `evidence.insert_id`, `evidence.deployment`, `evidence.future`, `evidence.call_id`, `evidence.field`, `evidence.value`, `evidence.hypothesis`, `evidence.limit`.
83|    - Diagnosis:
84|      - `diagnosis.schema`, with the JSON path of the problem (`diagnosis.schema: action: 'type' is a required property`). Argument-validation errors inside `diagnosis` use this rule, not `args.schema`.
85|      - `diagnosis.evidence`
86|      - `diagnosis.coverage`
87|      - `diagnosis.category` (includes `unknown` without `escalate`)
88|      - `diagnosis.action` (method outside the allowlist; empty `escalationSummary`)
89|      - `diagnosis.update_mask` (mask outside the method's fields, or patch keys outside the mask)
90|      - `diagnosis.resource`
91|      - `diagnosis.incident` (`incidentId` or `deployment`)
92|      - `diagnosis.component`, listing the contract's component IDs
93|      - `diagnosis.hypothesis`
94|      - `diagnosis.verification` (missing, or a tripwire not of this deployment)
95|      - `diagnosis.none_after_resume`
96|    - Other: `reads.cap`, `tool.unknown`, `tool.name`, `tool.error`, `args.schema` (with the JSON path).
97|26. **`set_hypotheses`.** Items are `{id, statement, wouldConfirm, alternative}`, all four required. IDs match `^H[1-9][0-9]*$` and are unique. 2–4 items, at least one alternative. Replacing the set keeps evidence whose hypothesis ID remains.
98|27. **`record_evidence`.**
99|    - **Log source:** the insertId exists, its timestamp is ≤ now, and it routes (via `Registry.route`) to the incident's deployment or to a sibling queried in this session (via `query_logs` on it, or `compare_siblings`). There is no other fallback.
100|    - **Tool source:** `callId` is an accepted read-tool call of this session. `field` is a dotted path into the result, where numeric segments index lists and a leading `result.` is stripped. `value` must match by JSON equality, with no coercion.
101|    - At most 3 items per hypothesis. IDs are `E<n>`, and `recordedAtTurn` is the session turn.
102|28. **`submit_diagnosis`** checks, in addition to spec §6.5:
103|    - The schema first. A schema problem always refuses, gates on or off. With gates on and no hypotheses yet, the order problem is reported first.
104|    - `incidentId` and `deployment` equal the incident's.
105|    - `component` is a component ID of the deployment's contract.
106|    - `hypothesis` is a current hypothesis.
107|    - For `propose`: a `connectorInstances.*` method needs the deployment's connector instance name, and a `jobInstances.*` method its job instance name, by exact match. The integration instance is never a valid resource. The patch keys are within `updateMask`.
108|    - `expectedVerification` is required for `propose` and `none`, and optional for `escalate`.

104|## Semantics
105|
106|10. **Opening and attaching.** `on_trip(event)`:
107|    - Every event, trip or recovery, first goes to `state.record_trip(event)`, which is what `tripwire_history` reads.
108|    - **Recovery:** if the deployment has an open incident, append a `recovery` timeline event (`detail: {"tripwire"}`) to it. Return `None`.
109|    - **Trip on a deployment with an incident not RESOLVED or ESCALATED:** attach to it. Add the tripwire to `tripwires` if it isn't there, append an `attached` event (`detail: {"tripwire"}`), and return its `Incident`.
110|    - **Any other trip:** create `Incident.from_trip(event, registry, clock.now())` with state OPEN, `pending = Pending("start", trigger="opened")` and an `opened` event, and return it.
111|
112|11. **`tick()`.** It works through `incidents()` in order:
113|    - **OPEN, or INVESTIGATING with `pending`:** set INVESTIGATING and run the pending segment synchronously to its end (no simulated time passes). Clear `pending` and handle the result (pin 12).
114|    - **NEEDS_INPUT:** check for a tripwire change (pin 13).
115|    - **AWAITING_APPROVAL:** nothing; it waits for `approve` or `reject`.
116|    - **APPLYING:** apply the proposal (pin 14).
117|    - **VERIFYING:** check verification (pin 15).
118|    - **RESOLVED and ESCALATED:** nothing.
119|
120|    Only running a pending segment makes model calls.
121|
122|12. **Handling a segment's result.**
123|    - Every result appends its `transcript_id` to `transcript_ids` if it isn't already there, and adds a `segment` event with status, reason and turns.
124|    - **`submitted`/`propose`:**
125|      - read the target with `reader.get(resource)`;
126|      - create a `Proposal` with `seq = len(proposals) + 1` and that `resource_version`;
127|      - move to AWAITING_APPROVAL with a `proposal` event (hash, seq).
128|    - **`submitted`/`none`:** call `verifier.start(..., changed_resource=None)`, move to VERIFYING, add `verification_started`.
129|    - **`needs_input`/any reason:**
130|      - move to NEEDS_INPUT with that `reason`;
131|      - set `paused_at = now` and `paused_snapshot = {tw: status}` for each tripwire in `tripwires`, read from `evaluator.status()`;
132|      - set `diagnosis` when the reason is `escalated`;
133|      - add a `needs_input` event.
134|
135|13. **Resuming on a tripwire change.**
136|    - On each tick, a NEEDS_INPUT incident compares `{tw: evaluator.status()[deployment][tw] for tw in tripwires}` with `paused_snapshot`.
137|    - It resumes, in the same tick, only when a tripwire that was `tripped` in `paused_snapshot` is now `ok`: `Pending("resume", message=<pin 21>, trigger="tripwire")`, run as in pin 11.
138|    - A trip while paused (a new tripwire attached, or an `ok` one tripping) only adds an `attached` event. It does not resume, and `paused_snapshot` is not updated. The next resume message lists it under `changes` (`none -> tripped` for a newly attached tripwire).
139|    - Anything else means no model call. (Amended 2026-11-01 after the Session A pre-flight: F2's canary trips about 5 minutes after the pause, and resuming on it cost a model call and broke T7's one-hour quiet window.)
140|
141|14. **Approve, reject, apply.**
142|    - **`approve(id, hash, by)`:**
143|      - The incident must be AWAITING_APPROVAL and `hash` its latest proposal's. Otherwise it raises `ValueError` and records nothing.
144|      - It records the approval in the `ApprovalStore`, moves to APPLYING and adds an `approved` event.
145|      - The apply happens on the next tick.
146|    - **`reject(id, hash, by, notes)`:**
147|      - It makes the same checks and records the rejection.
148|      - The incident moves to INVESTIGATING with `Pending("reopen", message=<pin 21>, trigger="rejection")` and a `rejected` event (notes).
149|      - The reopen runs on the next tick. A rejection is not a failed attempt.
150|    - **APPLYING, in `tick`:** `executor.apply(incident, proposal)`. The outcomes:
151|      - **Success:**
152|        - call `state.record_change(deployment, {at, method, resource, updateMask, patch, proposal_hash, approver})`;
153|        - call `verifier.start(..., changed_resource=resource)`;
154|        - move to VERIFYING with an `applied` event.
155|      - **`Conflict`:** pending reopen with trigger `conflict`, state INVESTIGATING, a `conflict` event. Not an attempt.
156|      - **`InvalidPatch`:** pending reopen with trigger `invalid_patch`. Not an attempt.
157|      - **`ApplyError`:** `failed_attempts += 1` and an `apply_failed` event. At 2 attempts, the incident goes ESCALATED with a postmortem; otherwise it gets a pending reopen with trigger `apply_failed`.
158|      - **`NotApproved`:** propagates, because it means a bug.
159|
160|15. **Verification.**
161|    - **`start`:**
162|      - the target is `diagnosis.expectedVerification.tripwire`, with `started = now` and `deadline = now + seconds`;
163|      - with `changed_resource`, the component is the deployment's component whose `resource_names` value equals it, and the verifier calls `evaluator.enter_change_point(deployment, component, duration_s=contract.changePoint.durationSeconds, overrides=contract.changePoint.overrides)`;
164|      - `none` arms no change point.
165|    - **`check`:** returns `verified` if `evaluator.status()[deployment][target] == "ok"`; otherwise `failed` if `now >= deadline`; otherwise `pending`.
166|      - The check is status-based, so a tripwire that recovered before the check verifies at once (T7).
167|      - A target the incident never tripped also verifies at once. The gates allow any tripwire of the deployment (spec §6.5 rule 5); accepted for the MVP.
168|    - **In `tick`:**
169|      - `verified`: RESOLVED with a postmortem and a `verified` event.
170|      - `failed`: `failed_attempts += 1` and a `verification_failed` event. At 2 the incident goes ESCALATED with a postmortem; otherwise it gets a pending reopen with trigger `verification_failed` and moves to INVESTIGATING.
171|
172|16. **`reply` and `close`.**
173|    - `reply` works only from NEEDS_INPUT with a message that isn't empty after stripping. Otherwise it raises `ValueError` and makes no model call.
174|    - It sets `Pending("resume", message=<pin 21>, extra_turns=extra_turns, trigger="reply")` and moves to INVESTIGATING. The next `tick()` runs it.
175|    - The segment gets `resume_turns + extra_turns` turns, so a `budget` pause resumes whether or not turns were granted.
176|    - `close` works only from NEEDS_INPUT, otherwise `ValueError`. It moves to ESCALATED with a `closed` event (by, note) and a postmortem.
177|
178|17. **Postmortem.**
179|    - It is built when an incident reaches RESOLVED or ESCALATED and stored on the record.
180|    - `category`, `root_cause` (the diagnosis `summary`) and `action` (`type`, `method`, `resource`, `updateMask`, `patch`) come from `record.diagnosis` and are `None` when it is absent.
181|    - `timeline` is `record.timeline`. Event kinds:
182|      - `opened`, `attached`, `recovery`, `segment`, `needs_input`;
183|      - `resumed`, with `detail.trigger` ∈ {`reply`, `tripwire`, `rejection`, `conflict`, `invalid_patch`, `apply_failed`, `verification_failed`} and `detail.message`;
184|      - `proposal`, `approved`, `rejected`, `conflict`, `applied`, `apply_failed`;
185|      - `verification_started`, `verified`, `verification_failed`, `closed`, `escalated`.
186|    - A `resumed` event is added whenever a pending `resume` or `reopen` segment starts.
187|
188|18. **`Executor.apply`, in order.**
189|    1. **Approval.** `approvals.approval_for(proposal.hash)` must exist with a matching `incident_id`; otherwise raise `NotApproved`. Nothing is journaled.
190|    2. **Concurrency.** Read the resource (deployer). If `resource_version(r) != proposal.resource_version`, raise `Conflict`. Nothing is journaled.
191|    3. **Steps.**
192|       - `*.patch`: the body holds the `update_mask` fields from `proposal.patch`.
193|         - For `parameters`, start from the resource's current list and set each proposed parameter's `value` by `displayName`, then send the full list.
194|         - A `displayName` not on the resource raises `InvalidPatch`, with nothing journaled.
195|       - `*.restart`: two steps, `{"enabled": false}` then `{"enabled": true}`, each with mask `enabled`.
196|       - `connectorInstances.runOnDemand`: body `{"connectorInstance": <resource read in step 2>}`.
197|       - `jobInstances.runOnDemand`: body `{}`.
198|       - Every connector patch body carries `integrationVersion` from the resource read in step 2; the mock returns 400 without it.
199|    4. **`intent`:** `{type, proposal_hash, approval_id, incident_id, method, resource, resource_version, steps: [{call, update_mask, body}], at}`, durable before any write.
200|    5. **`started`:** `{type, proposal_hash, at}`.
201|    6. **Each step:** the API call, then `step` `{type, proposal_hash, index, at}`.
202|    7. **`terminal`:** `{type, proposal_hash, outcome: "applied" | "already_applied" | "error", api_calls, detail, at}`.
203|
204|    A `ChronicleError` on a step writes `terminal` with outcome `error` and raises `ApplyError`. The concurrency check runs once, before the first write; the restart macro's own version bumps are not compared.
205|
206|19. **`Executor.recover()`.**
207|    - It handles every `intent` with no `terminal` for its `proposal_hash`, oldest first: it re-reads the resource and decides by method.
208|    - **Patch:** done if every masked field shows the proposed value. Parameters compare each proposed `displayName`'s value as a string; a `PASSWORD` parameter counts as done when the resource version has moved past the intent's.
209|    - **Restart:**
210|      - `enabled: false`: send only `{"enabled": true}`;
211|      - `enabled: true` with the version or `updateTime` unchanged since the intent: run both steps;
212|      - `enabled: true` with it changed: done.
213|    - **runOnDemand:** run it once more. This is at-least-once, because a run leaves no trace on the resource and an extra run is harmless.
214|    - **Done:** write `terminal` `already_applied` with `api_calls: 0`.
215|    - **Otherwise:** write `started`, run the remaining steps with `step` records, and write `terminal` `applied`. `integrationVersion` comes from the fresh read.
216|    - `recover` does not touch incidents.
217|
218|20. **Identities.**
219|    - The ToolSet's client and the manager's `reader` use `obs-reader`; the executor's client uses `deployer`.
220|    - T3 makes the same patch call with an `obs-reader` client and expects 403.
221|
222|21. **Messages (exact text).** Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with `Z`. Tests may assert these strings appear in the next model request's input.
223|    - Tripwire change: `Tripwire state changed since the pause at {paused_at}: {changes}. Current: {current}.`
224|      - `changes` is `; `-joined: `{tw} {old} -> {new}` for each tripwire in `paused_snapshot` whose status changed, then `{tw} none -> tripped` for each tripwire attached since the pause, whatever its status now.
225|      - `current` is `; `-joined `{tw} {status}` over all of `tripwires`.
226|    - Reply: `Reply from {by}: {message}`
227|    - Rejection: `Rejected by {by}: {notes} Revise the proposal or escalate.`
228|    - Conflict: `Conflict: {resource} changed since the proposal (version {expected} -> {actual}). Read it again before proposing.`
229|    - Invalid patch: `Apply refused: {problems joined by "; "}.`
230|    - Apply failed: `Apply failed: {detail}.`
231|    - Verification failed: `Verification failed: {tripwire} on {deployment} was not ok within {seconds} s of {started_at}. Investigate again.`

104|## Semantics
105|
106|10. **Opening and attaching.** `on_trip(event)`:
107|    - Every event, trip or recovery, first goes to `state.record_trip(event)`, which is what `tripwire_history` reads.
108|    - **Recovery:** if the deployment has an open incident, append a `recovery` timeline event (`detail: {"tripwire"}`) to it. Return `None`.
